messages:
maria.chen: Heads-up — I'm preparing the TF changes to onboard partner DC via a BGP peering over our TGW attachment. Putting the plan here for quick eyes before I open the PR. main items: peer ASN, advertised prefixes, route filters, and where to store the BGP MD5 key.

maria.chen: planned flow: create aws_vpn_connection (dynamic routing), attach to tgw, update tgw route table to propagate to app attachments, add route filter on partner side (they asked for explicit prefixes).

maria.chen: snippet I'm testing locally:
```hcl
resource "aws_vpn_connection" "partner_bgp" {
  customer_gateway_id = var.partner_cgw_id
  transit_gateway_attachment_id = aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment.tgw_attach.id
  type = "ipsec.1"
  bgp_asn = var.local_bgp_asn
  tunnel1_inside_cidr = "169.254.10.0/30"
}
```

maria.chen: question for infra: where do we want the MD5 pre-shared key? put it in Secrets Manager encrypted with the account KMS and reference via data "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" in TF, or use SSM Parameter (SecureString)? partner requires the key present in TF so we can advertise.

ashok.patel: 👍 prefer Secrets Manager. we already have role-based access for the tf runner module to read secretsmanager. SSM is fine but Secrets Manager gives rotation hook if we ever need it.

ashok.patel: also double-check TGW route propagation: you need to create a propagation from the VPN attachment into the TGW route table, and a route in the partner-facing TGW table for the prefixes they give. otherwise traffic won't flow to app attachments.

lina.kim: Quick note on TF: when you store the secret ARN as a var, make sure you don't put the raw key in state. use data source to read the value at apply time or use external secrets approach. we had a leak last year when someone put the plaintext in variables.tf :grimacing:.

raul.gomez: Can you paste the plan output once you run `terraform plan`? specifically I want to see the tgw_route_table_propagation and any changes to route tables. I'll check for unintended wide-ranging route adds.

infra-bot: terraform plan for branch bgp-onboard-1935: 
- aws_vpn_connection.partner_bgp will be created
- aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route_table_association.app-prop: +1
- aws_ec2_transit_gateway_route.app-to-partner: +1 (10.0.0.0/16 -> attachment)
- data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.bgp_key: read

maria.chen: plan attached. the partner provided prefixes: 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24. only advertising those.

ashok.patel: question — are we advertising 10.0.0.0/16 (prod) or only app subnets? partner said they want minimal prefix set. we should avoid adding supernet routes across the peering.

maria.chen: advertising only the app subnets (10.12.0.0/20, 10.13.0.0/20). I'll add explicit local prefix list and reference in the vpn_ha config.

raul.gomez: test suggestion: bring the BGP session up in staging and run bgp show routes on their router side (or get a pcap). Also validate community stripping — partner sometimes injects community tags that our edge filters don't expect.

lina.kim: I'll add a small TF validation step in CI that asserts the tgw route table entries don't have 0.0.0.0/0 being propagated. simple grep on plan output.

sre-oncall: Add monitoring: CloudWatch for tunnel state, and alert on BGP flaps >3 in 5m. Also record an SLO for session uptime for first 48h after cutover.

maria.chen: noted. I'll update the PR with: Secrets Manager reference, explicit prefix list, TGW propagation resource, CW alarms, and a short runbook for flaps.

ashok.patel: LGTM. ping me once PR is up and I'll do a quick review.

raul.gomez: I'll coordinate the partner test window after PR is merged.

maria.chen: Thanks all :rocket:
